course_name_original: Diseño Mecánico de Equipos y Tuberías en Plantas Industriales
course_name_en: Mechanical Design of Equipment and Piping in Industrial Plants
prerequisites: Urban Planning and Industrial Plant Installations (recommended, compulsory 1st-year course in the Master's Degree in Industrial Engineering)

learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving abilities in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Integrate knowledge and confront the complexity of forming judgments from incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons supporting them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Acquire learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
Possess adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of urban planning and infrastructure.
Project, calculate, and design products, processes, installations, and plants.
Lead, plan, and supervise multidisciplinary teams.
Conduct research, development, and innovation in products, processes, and methods.
Perform strategic planning and apply it to constructive, production, quality, and environmental management systems.
Technically and economically manage projects, installations, or industrial plants.
Be able to exercise functions of general management, technical management, and R&D&i project management in industrial plants.
Know, understand, and apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Engineer profession.
Design, build, and operate industrial plants.
Understand construction, building, installations, infrastructure, and urban planning in the field of industrial engineering.
Project and design electrical and fluid installations, lighting, HVAC, energy saving and efficiency, acoustics, communications, home automation and smart buildings, and security installations.

syllabus_topics: Piping networks: supports and flexibility analysis
Finite element calculation of piping networks (FEM-ANSYS)
Interpretation and comparison of FEM results
Calculation of pressure vessels according to current regulations
Finite element calculation of pressure vessels (FEM-ANSYS)
Interpretation and comparison of FEM results
Integration of industrial plant elements into a digital information model.

assessment_methods.method: Online questionnaires through Virtual Campus, MsForms or other applications
Assignments and projects developed in Classroom Practice sessions (group or individual)
Reports, memoirs or assignments related to Laboratory Practice sessions

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each assessment component. For non-presential students, assessment consists of a global online questionnaire (20%), a final exam on the entire course content (40%), and a practical exam on the work developed in practical classes (40%).
